cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you see lands clean.
cells.act: set one rule that makes the rest easier
cells.ask: Pick something whose whole shape is clear to you now, set a single rule from it — the line that makes the rest fall into place — and leave that rule where you work.
cells.core:
You can look at something tangled and see the shape of it. The pattern shows up before the reasons, and the reasons fall in line afterwards, cleanly enough that you no longer brace against the arrival. That is this side of you working as it should: direct, present, unhurried about the not-yet-known.

What you can give next is a shape other people can stand in. Pick something whose whole shape is clear to you now, set a single rule from it — the one line that makes the rest fall into place — and leave that rule where you work. You are not doing their work for them, only giving them the frame. When they can walk through what you saw with you nowhere around explaining, it has carried somewhere without you.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape. Now leave it where they can stand.

cells.tense: You will keep gathering until it is certain, and it will not be certain.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Pick what you are truly steering toward right now — the honest answer, not the safest — and turn toward it, dropping everything you have gathered that is not aiming there.
cells.core:
The assembling has grown past what seeing needs. You keep adding angles, more evidence, more of the shape, and the shape gets larger without getting clearer, until standing back far enough to take all of it in puts you nowhere near the thing itself. The gathering is no longer serving you.

What would come back is a plain wanting, pointed. Not a strategy — the thing you would be sorriest to lose. Face it, in your own words, and steer by it. Then let everything you have collected that is not aiming there drop away, and take a small step toward what remains. Perceiving the shape is not the destination by itself; it is for walking toward something.
cells.sheetLine: You gathered the whole map and stopped walking.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that closed behind you, waiting for someone to open it.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Choose one step you have been holding — the one whose ending you cannot already see — and take it, letting clarity arrive afterward rather than before.
cells.core:
Standing here, your own read of a thing arrives and it does not get used. Instead you go looking for someone else to confirm it, and the confirmation keeps not quite coming, because no one sees what you see. Fog is filling the space where your own sense of a thing used to stand.

What you can do is smaller than getting the sight back — it is just taking one step while still unsure. Choose one step you have been holding, the one whose ending you cannot already see, and take it, letting clarity arrive afterward. You do not need the whole road lit. The first steps are mostly memory, and you have walked this far already.
cells.sheetLine: Light comes after the step, not before it.

cells.tense: You are already writing in this room, and your hand is off the pen.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Take one decision from this month you shrugged off as a hunch and trace it back to what you spotted first — that credit is yours, and only you can return it.
cells.core:
Decisions keep turning out well in ways you did not plan. You call a move a guess, and it turns out to be the right one. Somewhere in you the read is happening — clean, accurate, arriving before the reasons — and the part of you that takes credit for the outcome is not the part that did the spotting.

What is wanted here is credit given where it is due, without keeping a ledger. Pick one decision from the last month that went well and you shrugged off, and trace it back to what you actually noticed before you made it. That is not bragging; it is fair return on something you have been loaning out at no cost. Do it once and you will start catching the sight before it surprises you.
cells.sheetLine: The sight is yours. Start signing for it.
